items/item_spray_paint.json: A dented aerosol can in Prismatik house colours, the label worn down to the hazard diamond. PRISMATIK. ONE CAN. EVERY COLOUR. A mixing head draws from four pigment cells and a white, and the collar clicks through the range as you turn it. It rattles when you pick it up. That's the only gauge it has.
items/item_cryocell.json: A slab of matte ceramic no bigger than a footlocker, a padded harness folded flat against the back. It radiates cold you can feel through your jacket. Stamped along the seam: ZENITH ENTERPRISES CRYOCELL. No plumbing, no permit, no grid draw. Sling it on and what's inside stays hard-frozen.
items/item_lucky_flashlight.json: Two-Cell's torch, rubber-armoured, "2-CELL" gouged into the barrel. The lens is cracked clean across and couldn't care less. Grady swears it has never left him in the dark, and it sips power: one cell lasts twice as long as any shop light. LIGHT to switch on, UNLIGHT to save it, RELOAD when it dies.
items/item_pyre_projector.json: A shoulder tank in unpainted steel, a braided feed line, and a nozzle that's mostly heat shielding. The gauge is analogue, because a needle can be read through smoke. Stencilled down the tank: VULCAN ORDNANCE PYRE-3. Scratched into the paint under it: IT DOES NOT KNOW WHAT YOU MEANT.
items/item_truck_spares.json: A steel box with a hinged lid and a handle worn smooth, packed the way people pack things they hope never to open: hose in three diameters, jubilee clips, brake line, emitter tape, fuses of the wrong rating, and a tube of something that seals anything. Heavy in the way that annoys you every mile.
items/item_orme_shortsword.json: The Trueline is Vessa Orme's own pattern: a straight, honest, slightly overweight shortsword with nothing clever about it. She makes one a week and won't be hurried. The circle worn flat on one side goes on all of them. The signature under the guard she cuts by hand, only into the good ones.
items/item_furn_fridge_glacier400.json: Scratched white enamel, twin doors, a magnetic seal that still bites. GLACIER 400 is stamped across the front in the confident sans-serif of a manufacturer that went bankrupt three product cycles ago. Every third kitchen in the city has one, inherited and never fully forgiven.
items/item_arc_lance.json: A metre of insulated spine ending in a forked emitter, a capacitor bank clamped along the shaft in four fat segments that whine up the scale as they charge. Kolvig built it for cutting rebar out of drowned foundations, which is why the grip is a full hand of rubber. It smells like a storm coming.
items/item_raw_tobacco_crop.json: A pressed bale of green leaf, strapped with wire and still smelling of the field. Nothing about it's illegal, which is why the frontier grows it: it rides in a hold in plain sight, and no badge has ever asked a pilot where his tobacco came from. Cure it down and it's smokable.
items/item_macaroni.json: A half-kilo box of little elbows, every one identical, pressed out by a machine that has been pressing out elbows since before the Handoff. There's a cartoon child on the front holding a bowl, drawn in a style nobody has drawn in for sixty years. It cooks up honest enough.
items/item_signal_decoder.json: A drone core reflashed into something it was never asked to be, wired to a fragment of Architect substrate and packed into a case that used to hold a glucose meter. It doesn't display anything. It gets warm, and its whine changes pitch when there's something nearby to listen to.
items/item_truck_engine.json: A diesel long-block on a steel pallet, shrink-wrapped and stencilled with a six-digit part number and a warning in two languages. Somebody has chalked a date on the block. It weighs what an engine weighs: it goes where a forklift takes it and stays there until somebody bolts it into something.
items/item_furn_microwave_pulsebox.json: A beige counter-top box with HOBLINE PULSEBOX embossed on the door and a dial that only reliably distinguishes between not enough and far too much. The turntable motor works. It hums at a pitch that gets into your teeth, and it'll make anything warm and nothing good.
items/item_furn_fridge_polaris.json: Brushed alloy, a shelf array that reconfigures itself around whatever you put in it, and an interior glow that comes on a half-second before the door's open, like it's been expecting you. The plate reads POLARIS EXECUTIVE. It's polite, it's efficient, and it is keeping track.
items/item_soylent_manyhappy.json: A foil pouch in a colour the others don't come in, a deep iridescent bronze, with no cartoon and no exclamation marks. MANY HAPPY RETURNS is printed small and centred, and under it, smaller: ISSUED ONCE ANNUALLY PER REGISTERED INSTANCE. The straw is the rigid kind, taped on straight.
items/item_bbq_sauce.json: A squat jar of sauce the colour of old brick, thick enough to stand a spoon in. The label is a strip of tape with MALCOLM'S on it in marker, and under it, smaller, in the same hand: it's fine. Apple butter, chipotle behind it, and a warmth that arrives four seconds late.
items/item_wb_mutagen_raw.json:
A flask drawn straight off the Pool and stoppered where it stood, the colour of a bruise and warm through the glass. It hasn't settled and it hasn't been tested.

Wick Ollam will tell you at length what it does to somebody who drinks it at this stage, and she won't sell you one.
items/item_pry_deck.json: A hobbyist breach kit built out of whatever the last owner had lying around: a cracked tablet shell, hand-soldered leads, and a fan that screams the moment you ask it for anything. The seller's label, stuck on crooked, reads TWO-CELL SUPPLY: SOLD AS SEEN. It gets a signal in. It won't enjoy it.
items/item_arc_cell.json: A brick of stacked supercapacitors in a ribbed grey shell, heavier than it has any right to be. The charge indicator on the end cap reads full, or reads nothing, and has no opinion about anything between. Handling instructions are moulded into the plastic in six languages, all beginning DO NOT.
items/item_ration_cheese.json: Six identical squares in a paper sleeve, each a colour that doesn't occur in dairy. Ration issue, and the sleeve says PROCESSED CHEESE FOOD PRODUCT rather than risk the word cheese alone. It melts faster than the real thing, which is either its one virtue or the worst thing about it.
items/item_kettleman_no4.json: A long-barrelled revolver in a finish that was once blueing and is now the memory of it. The Kettleman was issued to transit guards by the crate, which is why every third pawn shop has one and none are worth anything. Six shots, no safety, a trigger pull like dragging a chair over gravel.
items/item_pink_slab.json: An inch and a half thick, pale as a scar, with a fat cap on one side you could set your watch by. The wrapper says PORKY PORK PORK in three colours, two more assurances than honest pork has ever needed. Nobody at the counter will tell you what it came off, and you've learned not to ask.
items/item_raw_cannabis_crop.json: A bale of unsorted flower, cut wet and pressed too soon, sweating gently inside its wrap. It's entirely legal and it announces itself from thirty feet, which makes it the honest man's cargo and the cheapest thing on the Reach's books. Trim and cure it and you have loose leaf worth rolling.
items/item_tidewell_diving_knife.json: A short, thick blade with a blunt prying tip and a grip moulded for a gloved hand, coated against salt. Tidewell built it for cutting yourself out of a net at four metres, which is a specific way of saying it holds an edge when the rest of your kit has turned to rust.
